newsitem.title: USA: CBOT Dec wheat ends down, deliveries, weather cited.
newsitem.headline: CBOT Dec wheat ends down, deliveries, weather cited.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with nearby December hit hard by the posting Tuesday of 460,000 bushels of wheat for delivery on that contract, traders said.
Deferred months ended higher on cold weather in the U.S. winter wheat growing region that triggered fears some of the crop may be damaged, they said.

"There were new deliveries last night and there is some thought a previous stopper of deliveries may not be as strong as originally anticipated," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for FIMAT Futures.
The wheat market has been buoyed recently by perceptions that U.S. domestic mills have been the key stoppers of wheat posted for delivery on the December contract.
The December is slated to expire at 1201 CST Thursday and the market is expected to remain volatile through expiration, the traders said.
"E.D. and F. Man, who has been stopping wheat, is bear spreading and that's all it took. It was get out of the way," a trader said of the pit activity.
Wheat closed 9-1/4 cents per bushel lower to two cents higher, with December down 9-1/4 at $4.04-1/2.
Traders were mindful that the December wheat contract was vulnerable to violent price swings as Thursday, its last trading day, approaches.

"Last trading day for the December is coming up and it is super-thin (volume) in there," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co. "New crop was supported by cold weather and worries there may be a little damage to the crop."

Term Commodities bought one million bushels of July and Cargill Investor Services bought one million March, traders said. FIMAT Futures, Goldenberg Hehmeyer, LIT America and E.D. and F. Man sold one million bushels of March, traders said. SAK Futures sold 1.5 million March and sold one million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, slightly below the 13,878 traded Monday, according to the CBOT.

In wheat options, FIMAT Futures sold 1,500 May $3.50 puts at 11-1/2 cents, Continental Grain sold 250 March $7.00 puts at 15-1/2 to 16-1/4 cents and Tenco Inc bought 200 July $4.00 calls at 7-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,500 contracts, above the 6,616 contracts traded Monday.
